ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The motor lifts an object with a mass of $8\mathrm{kg}$ via a rope. The tension in the rope cannot exceed $120\mathrm{N}$, and the power of the motor cannot exceed $1200\mathrm{W}$.

1. To lift this object from rest to a height of $90\mathrm{m}$ in the fastest possible way (given that the object begins to ascend at a constant maximum speed as it approaches $90\mathrm{m}$), what is the required time?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The motor lifts an object with a mass of $8\mathrm{kg}$ via a rope. The tension in the rope cannot exceed $120\mathrm{N}$, and the power of the motor cannot exceed $1200\mathrm{W}$. To lift this object from rest to a height of $90\mathrm{m}$ in the fastest possible way (given that the object begins to ascend at a constant maximum speed as it approaches $90\mathrm{m}$), what is the required time?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use the given values m=8 kg, Tmax=120 N, Pmax=1200 W, h=90 m, starting from rest, and take g=10 m/s^2 as in the assigned method. The weight is mg=80 N. For the fastest lift, the motor should use the maximum allowed tension/power whenever possible. Initially the speed is small, so the power P=Tv is below the power cap while T=Tmax=120 N. The net upward force is 120−80=40 N, so the acceleration is a=40/8=5 m/s^2. The power cap is first reached when 120v=1200, so v=10 m/s. Time for this first stage: t1=10/5=2 s. Distance in this stage: x1=(1/2)(5)(2^2)=10 m. The remaining distance is 90−10=80 m. In the second stage, the motor runs at maximum power, so T=Pmax/v=1200/v. The equation of motion is 8 dv/dt=1200/v−80. Therefore dv/dt=(1200−80v)/(8v). For distance, dx/dv=v/(dv/dt)=8v^2/(1200−80v). Set ∫ from v=10 to vf of 8v^2/(1200−80v) dv =80. Solving this gives vf≈14.92 m/s, close to the limiting maximum speed 1200/80=15 m/s. For time in this stage, dt/dv=1/(dv/dt)=8v/(1200−80v). Thus t2=∫ from 10 to 14.92 of 8v/(1200−80v) dv ≈5.75 s. Total time is t=t1+t2≈2+5.75=7.75 s.

raw_record.final_cot:
Use the given values m=8 kg, Tmax=120 N, Pmax=1200 W, h=90 m, starting from rest, and take g=10 m/s^2 as in the assigned method. The weight is mg=80 N. For the fastest lift, the motor should use the maximum allowed tension/power whenever possible.

Initially the speed is small, so the power P=Tv is below the power cap while T=Tmax=120 N. The net upward force is 120−80=40 N, so the acceleration is a=40/8=5 m/s^2. The power cap is first reached when 120v=1200, so v=10 m/s. Time for this first stage: t1=10/5=2 s. Distance in this stage: x1=(1/2)(5)(2^2)=10 m.

The remaining distance is 90−10=80 m. In the second stage, the motor runs at maximum power, so T=Pmax/v=1200/v. The equation of motion is 8 dv/dt=1200/v−80. Therefore dv/dt=(1200−80v)/(8v).

For distance, dx/dv=v/(dv/dt)=8v^2/(1200−80v). Set ∫ from v=10 to vf of 8v^2/(1200−80v) dv =80. Solving this gives vf≈14.92 m/s, close to the limiting maximum speed 1200/80=15 m/s.

For time in this stage, dt/dv=1/(dv/dt)=8v/(1200−80v). Thus t2=∫ from 10 to 14.92 of 8v/(1200−80v) dv ≈5.75 s.

Total time is t=t1+t2≈2+5.75=7.75 s.
